findings.title: Delete menu item can never render for list-view rules (rulerRule is undefined)
findings.body: The Delete item is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule`. After this PR the alert list view intentionally no longer fetches ruler rules, so `rulerRule` is always `undefined` there, which means users can never delete a rule from the new rule list even though `canDelete` is now computed from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and the caller (`RuleActionsButtons.V2`) ignores the `rule` argument entirely (`handleDelete={() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)}`). The whole point of adding the Grafana-Prom delete ability is defeated. The guard (and the `handleDelete(rule: RulerRuleDTO, ...)` prop signature) should be relaxed so the item renders when `canDelete` is true and the identifier is known. Note that the new GrafanaGroupLoader test asserting exactly 4 menu items (no Delete) hard-codes this regression.

findings.title: Pause menu item still requires a ruler rule, so it is never shown in the list view
findings.body: The pause item is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` is truthy. Since the list view no longer loads ruler rules, `rulerRule` is `undefined` and the pause/unpause action silently disappears from the rule list, despite the newly added `grafanaPauseAbility` computation suggesting it should be available. Either `MenuItemPauseRule` needs to accept a Grafana Prometheus rule / rule identifier, or the computed Grafana pause ability is dead code that gives a false impression that pausing works.

findings.title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem inside mapped list
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` body, the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` without a `key`, while the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ... />` had one (and the other branches still pass `key={key}`). React will log a key warning for every render and, more importantly, cannot reconcile list items correctly when the filtered result set grows incrementally (items are appended via `setRules`), which can cause wrong item reuse/state and extra re-renders. Pass `key={key}`.

findings.title: Federated rule-group check dropped: federated rules become editable/deletable
findings.body: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now hard-codes `const isFederated = false` and the `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` call was removed when `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` was rewritten to delegate here. Previously rules belonging to a Mimir federated rule group (`source_tenants` present) were treated as immutable, so Edit/Delete/Pause were unsupported. With this change the UI will offer edit/delete for federated rules, and those write operations are not supported by the ruler for federated groups, so users will hit failures (or unintentionally modify a federated group). The federated check needs to be preserved, e.g. by passing the group (or a flag) into the hook rather than stubbing it out with a TODO.

findings.title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Export/Pause/Restore abilities
findings.body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` are gated on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, whereas the ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` which also matches Grafana recording rules. Since the list view now relies exclusively on this hook (ruler abilities resolve to false with no `rulerRule`), Grafana-managed recording rules can no longer be paused, exported with modifications, or restored from the rule list. If the intent was only to exclude recording rules from silencing, the alerting-only check should be limited to the `Silence` ability.

findings.title: `returnTo` query param dropped from rule view link
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` omits `returnTo`, so navigating into a rule from the list and then using the "return to previous" breadcrumb/button will no longer bring the user back to the filtered list page they came from.

findings.title: Test asserts exactly 4 menu items, locking in the missing Delete action
findings.body: The test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` both globally and on the folder, yet asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` and never checks `ui.menuItems.delete()` (the selector is defined but unused). This codifies the current behaviour where Delete (and Pause) are unreachable in the new list view because `AlertRuleMenu` still requires a `rulerRule` for those items. Once the menu is fixed the assertion will break; the test should explicitly assert the presence/absence of Delete and Pause so the regression is visible rather than baked in.

findings.title: Stale ruler-preload naming and comment after removing the ruler prefetch
findings.body: The ruler `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch was removed, but the surrounding comment ("This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded") and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` still describe ruler preloading. This is misleading for future readers who will look for ruler prefetching that no longer exists; rename/update to reflect that only the Prometheus group cache is populated.
